title: Write a clearer finding-title tip
tip: Prefer short titles that name the risky behavior directly, without exaggerating severity or hiding the concrete action that triggered the finding.

title: Add a minimal-evidence tip
tip: Show only the smallest excerpt needed to justify a finding, and redact unrelated secrets, tokens, paths, or personal data.

title: Add an actionable-remediation tip
tip: Remediation should tell the user what safer behavior to use instead of only saying that the original behavior is dangerous.

title: Add a false-positive review tip
tip: Before broadening a rule, add a safe counterexample that demonstrates which nearby behavior must remain allowed.

title: Add a narrow-rule design tip
tip: Prefer a narrow detection pattern tied to a concrete risky action over a broad keyword match that catches benign documentation.

title: Add a severity calibration tip
tip: Choose severity from plausible impact and required preconditions, not from how alarming a matched keyword sounds in isolation.

title: Add a safe-fixture writing tip
tip: A safe fixture should resemble the risky pattern closely enough to test precision while remaining clearly non-executable and harmless.

title: Add a suspicious-fixture writing tip
tip: Synthetic suspicious fixtures should isolate one behavior at a time so a failing test points to a specific detection rule.

title: Add a redaction tip
tip: Examples and reports should replace secrets and personal identifiers with obvious placeholders while preserving the structure needed to understand the finding.

title: Add a CLI-message clarity tip
tip: CLI findings should lead with rule ID and severity, then show concise evidence and one concrete next action.

title: Add an MCP least-privilege tip
tip: MCP examples should request only the tools and filesystem or network access needed for the demonstrated task.

title: Add a SKILL.md trust-boundary tip
tip: Treat instructions that fetch remote content, access credentials, or execute commands as explicit trust-boundary crossings that deserve narrow review.

title: Add a secure-example writing tip
tip: Documentation examples should demonstrate the safer alternative directly instead of reproducing a dangerous command that readers may copy.

title: Add a regression-test tip
tip: Every regression test should describe the behavior that previously failed and assert the smallest output needed to prevent the bug from returning.

title: Add a SARIF-result tip
tip: SARIF results should keep rule identifiers stable and point to the most specific source location available so downstream tools can group findings reliably.

title: Add an educational-warning tip
tip: Educational security warnings should explain why a pattern is risky and what precondition makes it dangerous, rather than relying on fear-based wording.
